fields.Short Description: A beach park since 1935 with a fishing pier, trails and camping. It has a mile of undeveloped beach, a pier for fishing, crabbing and wildlife watching, a nature center open most days, and a campground with hundreds of sites plus a few cabins built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. The nature trail closes from November through January, and pier fishing and camping cost extra.
fields.Name: Myrtle Beach State Park
fields.Address: 4401 S Kings Hwy, Myrtle Beach, SC 29575
fields.Hours Note: 6 AM–8 PM December through February. Parking is limited; arrive before 10 AM or after 2 PM on busy days.
fields.Price: $8 adults, $5 SC seniors, $4 ages 6–15, 5 and under free; pier fishing extra

fields.Short Description: Fast, narrated dolphin cruises of 1.5 to 2 hours from Little River. The boats run up the Intracoastal Waterway, past barrier islands and out through the jetty into the Atlantic to look for wild bottlenose dolphins. Sea Thunder boards at 1522 Watson Ave and Sea Screamer at 4499 Mineola Ave. The company offers a dolphin sighting guarantee; check its terms.
fields.Name: Sea Thunder and Sea Screamer
fields.Hours Note: Cruising daily in season (2026 season began March 21). Book online up to an hour before departure.

fields.Short Description: Boat tours through the Murrells Inlet salt marsh: birdwatching and shelling eco tours, history cruises and sunset cruises.
fields.Name: Visit Murrells Inlet Cruises & Tours

fields.Short Description: A 1.5-hour dolphin watch cruise leaving the MarshWalk dock in Murrells Inlet on a 46-foot boat with covered and open decks and a restroom. Marine science students or a naturalist narrate, and snacks and drinks are sold on board. It suits families and anyone after a relaxed outing; sightings aren't guaranteed. Kayak and paddleboard rentals are also available.
fields.Name: Express Watersports Dolphin Watch
fields.Hours Note: Office open Mon–Sat 10 AM–5 PM. Tours run on a seasonal schedule; book online.

fields.Short Description: A riverfront walk along Front Street with boat tours, museums and a marina.
fields.Name: Georgetown Harborwalk

fields.Short Description: PonTiki runs daily party boat cruises on the Intracoastal Waterway with music, dancing and drinks included. Public cruises last two hours, private cruises run two to eight hours, and the largest boat holds up to 47 passengers. Outside drinks are not allowed. Guests should be of drinking age.
fields.Name: PonTiki Myrtle Beach
fields.Hours Note: Seasonal schedule; check the contact page

fields.Short Description: A beach, marsh boardwalk, birding and nature center, home to Atalaya Castle. Three miles of beach have a dog-friendly south end, a freshwater lake is a good spot for seeing alligators, and birders can look for more than 300 species. There is a campground too. The nature center's marsh boardwalk was closed for construction when we last checked the park's site, so confirm before you go.
fields.Name: Huntington Beach State Park
fields.Hours Note: Open until 9 PM during Daylight Saving Time. Parking can fill on weekends; arrive before 10 AM or after 2 PM.
fields.Price: $8 adults, $5 SC seniors, $4 ages 6–15, 5 and under free

fields.Short Description: An exotic petting farm inland in Conway with more than 200 animals, from goats and llamas to sloths and lemurs, and hands-on encounters for families. Visits are by appointment.
fields.Name: Wild Woods Farm

fields.Short Description: Guided or on-your-own kayak and paddleboard trips through the Cherry Grove marsh, out to undeveloped Waties Island and along the Waccamaw River. Rentals too.
fields.Name: Great Escapes Kayaking Expeditions
fields.Address: 1603 Highway 17 S, North Myrtle Beach, SC 29582

fields.Short Description: Sightseeing and dolphin cruises from Little River.
fields.Name: Getaway Adventures Dolphin Tour

fields.Short Description: Waites Island is an undeveloped barrier island of more than 1,000 acres at the northern tip of South Carolina, between Cherry Grove and Sunset Beach. There are no roads: visitors arrive by guided horseback ride, kayak or paddleboard through the salt marsh. Bald eagles, ospreys and herons live there, and dolphins and sea turtles are seen in summer.
fields.Name: Waites Island
fields.Address: Cherry Grove, North Myrtle Beach, SC 29582
fields.Hours Note: Guided trips by Inlet Point Plantation Stables and Great Escapes Kayak Expeditions; reservations required

fields.Short Description: Dolphin-watch and sunset cruises from the MarshWalk. The marina also runs marsh eco and birdwatching tours, history and ghost cruises, pirate adventures and wine-sampling sails, plus fishing trips and rentals of pontoons, skiffs, kayaks and jet skis. It suits families and couples; see the website for the current schedule.
fields.Name: Crazy Sister Dolphin Cruises
fields.Hours Note: Cruise schedule changes through the year. Book online or call (843) 651-3676.

fields.Short Description: Socastee Recreation Park is a 91.5-acre Horry County park with multi-purpose fields, picnic areas, a disc golf course, walking trails and a playground. It is a free place for families to spend a few hours away from the oceanfront.
fields.Name: Socastee Recreation Park
fields.Hours Note: County parks are open dawn to dusk

fields.Short Description: This 160-acre park in Little River has baseball, softball and soccer fields, freshwater ponds, walking trails, two playgrounds, picnic shelters and the Cypress Nook disc golf course. It hosts youth tournaments and team events, and is a free place to stretch your legs, play a round or let the kids run.
fields.Name: North Myrtle Beach Park & Sports Complex

fields.Short Description: A 16,000-acre coastal research reserve near Georgetown that you can only visit on a guided tour or program. Options include a two-hour weekday tour, a longer seasonal Saturday tour, and a four-mile hike to the North Inlet salt marsh, along with programs such as birding and trail rides. More than 70 cultural sites, including the Baruch family homes, cemeteries and former enslaved people's cabins, tell the property's history. Tours are booked through the website.
fields.Name: Hobcaw Barony
fields.Hours Note: Discovery Center open daytime. Guided tours Mon–Fri at 9:30, 10:30, 1:30 and 2:30, and Saturdays at 10 AM; book ahead.

fields.Short Description: A waterfront boardwalk along the marsh, lined with live-music venues.
fields.Name: Murrells Inlet MarshWalk

fields.Short Description: This 70-acre Horry County park has seven miles of mountain biking and hiking trails near the Intracoastal Waterway. It is a good stop for riders and hikers who want a break from the beach, and it is run by the county as a public park.
fields.Name: Horry County Bike & Run Park
fields.Address: 150 Frontage Rd B-2, Myrtle Beach, SC 29579

fields.Short Description: Tiki Tours runs scenic cruises on the Intracoastal Waterway near Myrtle Beach aboard an 18-passenger tiki boat, including sunset cruises. It is a laid-back way to see the waterway with friends or family, and the boat is also booked for bachelor and bachelorette parties, corporate outings and other special occasions.
fields.Name: Tiki Tours of Myrtle Beach
fields.Address: 5843 Dick Pond Rd, Myrtle Beach, SC 29588
fields.Hours Note: Book ahead; call or check online for departure times

fields.Short Description: A reptile park beside Barefoot Landing in North Myrtle Beach, billed as one of the world's biggest homes for reptiles. Alongside alligators you'll see snakes, turtles and other animals, with some mammals and birds, such as lemurs, flamingos and a capybara, on view for limited times. Live shows let guests meet animals up close and learn about them. Check the website for current hours and tickets.
fields.Name: Alligator Adventure
fields.Address: 4604 Hwy 17 S, North Myrtle Beach, SC 29582

fields.Short Description: Sea Racer runs dolphin-watching cruises from the Big M Casino boat dock in Little River on a 70-foot boat with a 360-degree viewing area and room for up to 128 passengers. Tours last about 1.5 to 2 hours along the Little River and Myrtle Beach coastline. Dolphin sightings are not guaranteed.
fields.Name: Sea Racer Tours
fields.Hours Note: Seasonal: reopens March 15, 2027; check the schedule online

fields.Short Description: A sculpture garden since 1932, with live oaks, a wildlife trail and a lowcountry farm and zoo. Beyond the gardens there are seasonal exhibits, including a holiday train display and holiday market, and wellness events such as yoga in the gardens. General admission tickets are good for seven consecutive days, so a visit can be spread over several days.
fields.Name: Brookgreen Gardens
fields.Hours Note: Daytime gates close at 4:30 PM. No pets.
fields.Price: Adults $25, seniors $23, ages 4–12 $14, 3 and under free; tickets good for 7 days

fields.Short Description: Kayak (including fishing kayaks) and paddleboard rentals, plus surf lessons, in the Pawleys Island area. The family-run shop also rents surfboards and skim and body boards and sells surf apparel, including a kids' collection. It is open Monday through Saturday and has three locations.
fields.Name: Surf the Earth
fields.Address: 47 Da Gullah Way, Pawleys Island, SC 29585

fields.Short Description: An oceanfront promenade with piers, rides and summer live music.
fields.Name: Myrtle Beach Boardwalk

fields.Short Description: Dolphin trips from North Myrtle Beach.
fields.Name: Voyager Dolphin Cruises
fields.Address: 1525 13th Ave N, North Myrtle Beach, SC 29582

fields.Short Description: Vereen Memorial Gardens is an Horry County park on the waterfront in Little River with about three miles of nature trails and boardwalks. It is a quiet, free spot for a walk, bird watching and views over the marsh and waterway. Beach wheelchairs can be reserved through the county.
fields.Name: Vereen Memorial Gardens
fields.Hours Note: County parks are open dawn to dusk

fields.Short Description: Guided kayak tours of a cypress forest, the Murrells Inlet salt marsh and Huntington Beach State Park, plus kayak fishing trips. Book online for the meeting spot.
fields.Name: Black River Outdoors Center
fields.Hours Note: Guided kayak tours by reservation; book online or call (843) 546-4840.
fields.Price: Guided tours from $40 (2-hour salt marsh) to $130 (4-hour kayak fishing)

fields.Short Description: A big-cat and exotic-animal preserve offering hands-on wildlife encounters. Day and night safari tours feature tigers and wolves, and the animals include Bubbles, a rescued African elephant, Odin the liger, and chimp brothers Vali and Sugriva. Photo encounters, the Capybara Café and private group experiences are also offered. Tours are by reservation only.
fields.Name: T.I.G.E.R.S. / Myrtle Beach Safari
fields.Address: 851 Folly Ranch Ln, Myrtle Beach, SC 29588
fields.Hours Note: Open three days a week, by reservation only.

fields.Short Description: Plantation River Tours leaves from Wacca Wache Marina in Murrells Inlet on two river trips: the Waccamaw Lady, a 60-foot pontoon boat narrated by a local historian who covers the plantations' history, and the Waccamaw Cooter airboat tour of the Waccamaw, Black and Pee Dee rivers.
fields.Name: Plantation River Tours
fields.Address: Wacca Wache Marina, Murrells Inlet, SC
fields.Hours Note: Check the website for tour times

fields.Short Description: The Conway Riverwalk is a scenic promenade of roughly a mile along the dark Waccamaw River in downtown Conway. Along the way are historic markers, public artwork, a public park, a marina and a playground, so it works well for a family stroll after a visit to the Horry County Museum.
fields.Name: Conway Riverwalk

fields.Short Description: Splinter City is a 25-acre Horry County disc golf course in Myrtle Beach with two sets of tees. It is open daily and free to play, which makes it an easy low-cost activity for visitors who bring their own discs.
fields.Name: Splinter City Disc Golf Course
fields.Address: 3383 Splinter City St, Myrtle Beach, SC 29577
